editorial:
You follow Naruto as he chases missing-nin Mukade into ancient ruins, only to get blasted twenty years into the past. There he meets a young Minato Namikaze, the future Fourth Hokage, and joins a mission to stop Mukade from using a powerful leyline. The movie mixes time travel, ninja action, and a surprisingly emotional father-son connection without getting too heavy. It feels like a fast, colorful adventure that gives fans a rare look at Minato before he became a legend, while keeping Naruto’s usual loud energy front and center.

The action is quick and easy to follow, with plenty of jutsu battles and chase scenes. The animation looks sharp, especially during the big finale, and the pacing rarely slows down. On the downside, the story is pretty straightforward and some side characters do not get much to do. Still, if you want a fun Naruto side story with heart, this is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final battle, Naruto and Minato work together to stop Mukade from controlling the leyline. Mukade is defeated, but the energy threatens to pull everyone apart. Minato uses his space-time jutsu to send Naruto back to his own time. Naruto wakes up in the present with no memory of meeting his father, while Minato quietly realizes the boy he helped was his son. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Naruto carrying on without knowing the truth.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves anime adventures with time travel and emotional family moments.
